extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners developing blockchain-enabled AI systems (academics, industry developers in AI, blockchain, IoT and cybersecurity)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for designing, implementing, and assessing blockchain-based systems and infrastructure that support AI applications (storage, learning, deployment, consensus, and governance). Targets technical architects, researchers, and developers integrating blockchain with AI/ML.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced Data Security
rubrics_metrics.description: "Information held within blockchain is highly secure. Blockchains are very well known for storing sensitive and personal data in a disk-less environment. Blockchain databases hold data that are digitally signed..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use blockchain to ensure data are cryptographically signed, tamper-evident, and resilient. Prefer storing sensitive metadata or hashes on-chain rather than large raw datasets. Leverage blockchain for secure provenance and to reduce risk of centralized tampering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improved Trust on Robotic/AI Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Recording the decision making process of an AI system on a blockchain would increase transparency and it would gain public trust to understand the robotic decisions..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record decision footprints, logs, and audit trails to increase transparency and enable human auditing. Use blockchain to eliminate the need for third-party auditors in some swarm/collective scenarios. Balance the need for transparency with privacy constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective Decision Making (voting via blockchain)
rubrics_metrics.description: "In a robotic swarm ecosystem... Robots take decisions by voting and outcomes are determined by majority rules. Each robot can cast its vote in the form of a transaction..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represent votes/agreements as on-chain transactions to achieve verifiable consensus among agents. Use immutable transaction records for verification and repeated consensus rounds. Consider transaction latency and cost when designing voting frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralized Intelligence / Multi-agent Coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: "For taking smart high level decisions which involve multiple agents... different individual cybersecurity AI agents can be combined to provide fully coordinated security..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Architect systems as decentralized agents that share provenance and model artifacts via blockchain. Facilitate coordinated behaviors (e.g., scheduling, distributed detection) through shared ledgers while preserving autonomy of agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: High Efficiency via Decentralized Autonomous Agents (DAOs)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The integration of AI and blockchain technologies enables intelligent Decentralized Autonomous Agents (or DAOs) for automatic and fast validation of data/value/asset transfers among different stakeholders."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automate multiparty business processes using smart contracts to reduce multiparty authorization overhead. Evaluate efficiency gains versus overhead of on-chain operations; use permissioned or consortium chains for faster, lower-energy consensus when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Provenance and Authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralized AI systems suffer from risks that 'the data provenance and authenticity of the sources generating the data are not guaranteed' — blockchain can provide provenance and immutable histories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use blockchain to record metadata, provenance, and signatures of data sources so downstream AI models can trust inputs. Store hashes/metadata on-chain and raw data off-chain to balance cost and provenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traceability / Auditability of AI Lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: "Such platform can also be used to host a trusted trail of all records taken by AI algorithms before, during, and after the learning and decision making process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persist model training runs, datasets used, evaluation metrics, and deployment timestamps on-chain (or as hashes) to enable reproducibility, auditing, and explainability. Avoid putting mutable or sensitive raw data on-chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Decentralized Off-chain Storage with On-chain Hashes
rubrics_metrics.description: "Conventional blockchain is a very expensive medium for storing large amounts of data... To solve this problem, a decentralized storage medium is used for storing such data and hashes of the data are linked with the blockchain blocks or used within the blockchain smart contract code. Among the popular decentralized storage technologies are the Interplanetary File System (IPFS), Swarm, Filecoin, BigChainDB, Storj..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Store large files and datasets off-chain in decentralized storage and record their content-addressed hashes on-chain for integrity and discovery. Choose appropriate storage (IPFS, Filecoin, Storj) based on availability, retrieval guarantees, and cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharding and Swarming for Scalable Decentralized Storage
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sharding is the process of creating logical partitions of databases... The shards are further grouped together and their collected storage is supported by a group of nodes in the network in the form of swarms. Swarms reduce latency..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partition large datasets into shards and distribute across swarms to improve parallel access, reduce latency, and increase reliability. Use token-incentivized storage participation and consider data locality and redundancy for AI workloads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralized Data Management (metadata on-chain)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Decentralized data management schemes are envisaged to be deployed at node levels... decentralized data management schemes can put the metadata on the blockchain in order to maintain security and provenance of the data. The actual data could be stored in traditional large-scale storage systems..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put metadata, provenance, access-control records and pointers on-chain while storing payloads off-chain. Implement context-aware routing, temporal management, and token incentives to avoid unnecessary duplication and bandwidth overload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralized Learning Model Development
rubrics_metrics.description: "The decentralization of learning model development process is a feasible approach ... Decentralized learning algorithms take the input datasets from relevant swarms and shards and produce highly personalized learning models for each client... blockchain technologies can facilitate the maintenance of provenance of data as well as immutable history of learning models..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt federated or decentralized training paradigms that access local shards/swarms, preserve provenance, and support incremental model building. Use blockchain to record model versions, authorship, and provenance rather than storing model weights on-chain unless necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Deployment with Smart-Contract-Based Immutable Versioning
rubrics_metrics.description: "Smart contract based model deployment addresses these challenges by permanently recording the changes and maintaining the immutable versioning of different models."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use smart contracts to register, version, and authorize models for deployment; record provenance and deployment metadata on-chain. Ensure models are well-trained and tested before on-chain registration because smart contracts are effectively immutable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smart Contract Security and Verifiability
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper cites smart contract vulnerabilities and tools: "Smart contracts vulnerabilities: A call for blockchain software engineering?... Making smart contracts smarter... Securify: Practical security analysis of smart contracts... Smartcheck: Static analysis of ethereum smart contracts."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform static and formal analysis of smart contracts (e.g., Securify, Smartcheck), thorough testing, and security audits before deployment. Treat smart contracts as critical software components: follow secure development lifecycle and prepare for upgrade/escape mechanisms where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissioning and Blockchain Type Suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Blockchains are categorized as permissioned (private, consortium) or permissionless (public). The paper details trade-offs: openness, identity, transaction time, energy consumption, and security risk (51% attack).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select blockchain type by requirements: use public chains for openness and decentralization (but expect higher latency and energy cost); use private/consortium chains for known identities, low-latency transactions, and energy efficiency. Consider BaaS for rapid development and integration with cloud AI services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Blockchain Characteristics (suitability and trade-offs)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Public blockchains are easily accessible ... user identities and transactional privacy information on these blockchain are managed using anonymous and pseudonymous data ... Public blockchains need consensus of at least 51% validators ... large energy consumption ... transaction approval time ... typically a transaction on public blockchain is approved in 10 minutes or more..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public blockchains when maximal openness and censorship-resistance are needed, and when slower, higher-cost consensus is acceptable. Mitigate privacy concerns (pseudonymity) and be aware of 51% attack risks and energy use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private Blockchain Characteristics (suitability and trade-offs)
rubrics_metrics.description: "A private blockchain is managed by a single organization... permissioned systems ... comparatively faster due to known identities ... requires less complex mathematical operations ... transaction approval time on private blockchains usually remains lower than one second."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer private ledgers when participants are known/trusted, require high throughput and low-latency, and when privacy is required. Accept centralized governance trade-offs and design appropriate access controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium (Federated) Blockchain Characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: "Consortium blockchains are operated by a group of organizations... these blockchains operate as permissioned systems... a few authorized and trusted users can write the data on the blockchain... comparatively faster than public blockchains... consume less energy... transaction approval within one second."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consortium chains for cross-organization AI collaborations that need shared ledgers, controlled write permissions, and fast transactions. Design governance and membership rules carefully to prevent centralization of trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blockchain-as-a-Service (BaaS) Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cloud providers (Microsoft, Amazon, IBM) offer BaaS to develop, test, and deploy blockchain applications, enabling single-click provisioning and integration with cloud AI services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage BaaS for rapid prototyping and to combine cloud AI services with ledger capabilities, but evaluate vendor lock-in, compliance, and separation of concerns between cloud provider and consortium governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear vs Nonlinear (Multi-chain) Infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: "Single chain based blockchain architectures grow linearly... Single chain blockchains scale up slowly... Nonlinear blockchain architectures are implemented in the form of multichain architectures... parent-child chains, main-side chains, and parallel chains... facilitate execution of multiple interrelated or independent AI tasks..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose multi-chain architectures (sidechains, child chains, parallel chains) for scalability and for separating development/test nets from production. Use pegging/two-way peg techniques for cross-chain value transfers and plan for auditing and cross-chain consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus Protocol Selection and Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Consensus protocols (PoW, PoS, PBFT, PoET, proof-of-vote, etc.) affect security, energy use, throughput, and latency. Example: PoW requires solving complex mathematical problems and is energy-intensive; public chains using PoW need 51% validators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select consensus by threat model and performance needs: PoW offers strong decentralization at high energy cost and latency; permissioned settings can use PBFT or voting-based consensus for low-latency, low-energy operation. Consider hybrid or novel protocols for AI-specific workloads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalability and Real-time Performance Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: "Single chains scale up slowly and compromise the real-time performance of decentralized applications... These systems have multiple issues... Multi-chain architectures are not only scalable for real-time performance but also support diverse business scenarios and cross-chain value transfers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design for the expected throughput and latency of AI tasks. For real-time or near-real-time AI (robotics, swarm decisions), prefer permissioned or multi-chain designs and off-chain computation to meet performance constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy, Identity and Anonymity Trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Public blockchains manage identity via anonymous/pseudonymous data; private/consortium chains have known identities. Choice impacts privacy, auditability, and security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance privacy (e.g., GDPR) against auditability. For sensitive AI data (health, personal), prefer permissioned ledgers, selective disclosure, or zero-knowledge techniques; record only necessary metadata on-chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy Consumption / Environmental Cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Consensus mechanisms (e.g., PoW) can result in large energy consumption; permissioned consensus protocols consume less energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for environmental and operational costs in protocol selection. For sustainable AI/blockchain systems, prefer low-energy consensus (PoS, PBFT, PoET) in permissioned contexts or use energy-efficient public protocols where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immutability Constraints vs Data Mutability Needs
rubrics_metrics.description: "Considering the permanent nature of smart contracts, learning models need to be trained and tested well prior to deployment on blockchain." Also: 'Since AI applications usually operate in unconstrained environments therefore putting whole AI application components on blockchain is not a feasible choice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid storing mutable data or raw continually-updated datasets on-chain. Use off-chain training and keep only immutable hashes/records on-chain. Plan model governance and upgrade paths since smart contracts are often immutable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralized Optimization and Local Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: "The decentralized optimization leads to increased system performance by processing highly relevant data... The decentralized optimization is also beneficial when multiple strategies with different optimization objectives need to be run simultaneously across applications and systems."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design optimization tasks to operate locally on relevant shards/clients to reduce bandwidth and improve performance. Use the ledger to coordinate results, share best practices, and record proven optimization traces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate Use-cases for On-chain vs Off-chain Components
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper warns that "putting whole AI application components on blockchain is not a feasible choice" and suggests storing footprints (performance histories, successful search traces) on-chain instead of full components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Store provenance, model metadata, audit logs and successful traces on-chain; perform heavy computation (training, inference at scale) off-chain or at the edge. Use on-chain references to off-chain artifacts for integrity without incurring high cost or latency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provenance, Versioning and Model Sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Blockchain enables "immutable and highly secure versioning of learning models by maintaining provenance and historical aspects of data... model sharing between different AI applications becomes secure and more trustworthy since the developers can track the provenance and all footprints of any specific version of a model."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record model provenance, authorship, training configuration, and evaluation on-chain to enable trustworthy model sharing, benchmarking, and reuse. Use registries and access control to manage model lifecycle and provenance queries.
